links.note: Was 32688 (North-Seeking, South-Seeking). The leading true/false statement is that a magnet can be broken to get a single pole, which 32687 rules out.
Was 32684 (Lodestones and Artificial Magnets). Bringing the other end of magnet B towards the same end of A is Activity 4.5, the attraction/repulsion test in 32691.
Was 32684 (Lodestones and Artificial Magnets). Telling two magnets from an iron bar without any other material can only be done by repulsion, which 32691 establishes as the sole identifying test.
Was 32684 (Lodestones and Artificial Magnets). A ring magnet held up above another is like poles repelling - 32691.
Was 32686 (Two Definitions from One Table), which is magnetic against non-magnetic materials. Working out the polarity at each end of three arranged magnets uses the attract/repel rule of 32691.
Was 32692 (The Compass Needle Is a Magnet Too). Guessing the Earth's poles from a compass rests on 32688's claim that the Earth itself behaves like a giant magnet.
Was 32692 (The Compass Needle Is a Magnet Too). Making a sewing needle into a magnet by stroking is Activity 4.4 in 32690.
Was 32685 (Predict First, Then Test). The surest test is repulsion, and 32691 is where the chapter says attraction proves nothing on its own.
Was 32688 (North-Seeking, South-Seeking). North brought near South is the unlike-poles-attract half of 32691.
Was 32688 (North-Seeking, South-Seeking). North near North is the like-poles-repel half of 32691.

Was 32695 (How Poles Are Marked), which is about N/S markings and paint. The surviving statement is that the ends where attraction is strongest are the poles - 32687's iron-filing finding. Stem is truncated.
Was 32692 (The Compass Needle Is a Magnet Too). Putting paper between magnet and compass and finding the deflection unchanged is 32693 - the magnetic effect acts through non-magnetic materials.
Was 32684 (Lodestones and Artificial Magnets). What not to do to a magnet - heat it, hammer it, keep it near phones - is the care list in 32696.

Was 32693 (Magnetism Acts Through Wood and Glass), which is about the effect passing through a barrier. Pulling iron and steel out of mixed waste turns on the magnetic/non-magnetic split defined in 32686.
Was 32695 (How Poles Are Marked). Distinguishing a magnet from an identical iron bar is the repulsion test of 32691, since the iron bar is attracted by both poles.
Was 32695 (How Poles Are Marked). Filings crowding the ends and sparing the middle is Activity 4.2's observation in 32687.
Was 32688 (North-Seeking, South-Seeking). Testing magnet A's pole against each end of B is Activity 4.5's attract/repel reasoning in 32691.
Was 32686 (Two Definitions from One Table), which is the conclusion. The table being filled - object, material, prediction, observation - is Activity 4.1 itself, in 32685.
Was 32688 (North-Seeking, South-Seeking). Repeating the step with the South pole of the bar magnet and watching the needle is Activity 4.6 in 32692.
